newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end stronger, sharply outperform U.S..
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end stronger, sharply outperform U.S..

text.p: Canadian bonds ended stronger on Wednesday, outperforming U.S. issues as the market broke through key technical resistance levels amid foreign buying and optimism about the upcoming federal budget, dealers said.

"The charts have broken out," said Hank Cunningham, director of fixed income for First Marathon Securities Ltd. "I think there are a lot of people that decided to put flattening trades on here with the consensus very strong that we've seen the best of the short end," he said.
Canada's 30-year bond rose C$0.65 to C$110.90 to yield 7.080 percent.
The U.S. 30-year benchmark bond fell 12/32 to yield 6.75 percent. The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to 33 basis points from 42 basis points at Tuesday's close.

"People are putting on curve flatteners. People are buying Canada against the U.S. It's just been a great day," said a dealer at one bank-owned brokerage. "There was nothing specific about today except it was time. I can't specifically tell you why today was so magical," he said.
Among the factors helping Canada is growing speculation that the federal budget on February 18 will be well received by financial markets, analysts said.

Analysts also noted that Canada did not have to contend with the announcement of new supply that the U.S. market did. However, the Government of Canada will announce on Thursday details of the February 22 auction of 10-year bonds.
Buying of Canadian bonds came from both Canada and the United States, said one dealer.
In other news, the U.S. Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee left U.S. interest rates unchanged as many investors had expected.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 rose C$0.27 to C$104.22 to yield 6.412 percent.
The U.S. 10-year bond fell 4/32 to yield 6.47 percent.
It was the first time this year that the yield on the Canadian 10-year bond traded below the U.S. 10-year yield.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.88 percent against the U.S. bill which yielded 5.12 percent.
